note: The United States' national spirits. The ones with `start` describe the situation on 1 January 2000 and cite sources; the others are granted by the US focuses and decisions. Values are gameplay estimates.

spirits.name: The world's largest economy
spirits.description: The United States has been the world's largest national economy since around 1890, with the world's largest stock exchanges and high spending on research.

source.title: Wikipedia: Economy of the United States

spirits.name: The reserve currency
spirits.description: The US dollar is the world's foremost reserve currency.

source.title: Wikipedia: Economy of the United States

spirits.name: Military superpower
spirits.description: The US armed forces have the highest military expenditure in the world and global reach.
spirits.review_note: The source gives the 2025 expenditure (the world's highest); confirm that US military spending was also the world's highest in 2000.

spirits.name: The dot-com bubble
spirits.description: A stock-market bubble in internet companies built up in the late 1990s and peaked on 10 March 2000.

spirits.name: Homeland security
spirits.description: A cabinet department and new surveillance powers for domestic security.

spirits.name: Financial crisis
spirits.description: Banks fail, credit dries up and unemployment rises.

spirits.name: Bank rescue
spirits.description: Public money recapitalises the banks while the economy recovers.

spirits.name: Financial regulation
spirits.description: New rules and regulators for banks and consumer finance.

spirits.name: Shale boom
spirits.description: Horizontal drilling and fracking raise oil and gas output.

spirits.name: Industrial policy
spirits.description: Federal money for chips, clean energy and factories at home.

spirits.name: Expanded health coverage
spirits.description: Subsidised insurance and a wider Medicaid cover millions more people.

spirits.name: Third-party surge
spirits.description: A third party breaks the hold of the two major parties.
